lineage.mechanism: Project-Frankenstein 'Adaptive Visual Pipeline' used a fast detector/OCR/scene Stage 1 and a confidence/question-dependent VLM Stage 2. Adaptivity was routing/escalation adaptivity: confidence penalties and semantic-question triggers selected whether deeper perception was invoked.
lineage.important_boundary: No persistent user-specific classifier/prototype update loop, trusted-example admission, candidate promotion or rollback was found in this historical module.

lineage.mechanism: The old adaptive routing stack was explicitly deleted and replaced by FrankEye, a unified CPU-oriented vision module. The replacement commit reports 3.7 GiB VRAM freed by the broader voice/vision consolidation; treat that number as a historical implementation report, not an independently replicated benchmark.

Frozen-head FrankEye embeds Digital Retina v8 CNN as inference-only and combines it with DINOv2, hand-engineered visual features, OCR and face analysis. It is a reusable perceptual feature/evidence surface but does not itself establish the current FRANK 0.1 online personal learner contract.

Later Digital Retina added a genuinely learned pattern-library/dictionary family with nearest-neighbour/centroid-style readout and held-out dictionary-growth evaluation. This is learning/memory adaptivity rather than merely route selection, but the historical procedure was global/offline and oracle-seeded rather than the current user-scoped trusted online learner.

FRANK 0.1 intentionally recombines both ancestral ideas: cheap confidence/familiarity-based routing from the Project-Frankenstein path plus persistent prototype/tiny-readout learning from the later Retina path, now strengthened with user scope, open-set semantics, evidence tiers, bounded cyclic updates, candidate shadowing, rollback and replay.

new_findings.finding: Historical use of the word 'adaptive' is mechanism-ambiguous. In Project-Frankenstein it primarily meant adaptive compute escalation; in later Digital Retina it also meant a learned pattern/dictionary readout. These must not be merged into a single historical 'adaptive learner' claim.
new_findings.value: Prevents false earned-work credit and migration assumptions.

new_findings.finding: The old escalation engine already encoded the correct qualitative direction for current visual compute control: low confidence/complex semantic questions increase depth; text-rich/easy cases can stop early. The current MVC can reuse this as routing logic only after replacing hand thresholds with calibrated familiarity/open-set receipts where appropriate.

The March replacement proves a historical architecture discontinuity: the routing-adaptive module was deleted before the later learned-library Retina evidence. Therefore H1 must explicitly reconstruct/compose the desired behavior; it cannot assume frozen Project-Frankenstein already contains the complete user-adaptive learner.

The later Retina hard-set results reinforce that broad visual similarity/coverage is not a safe KNOWN gate. A Micro Visual Classifier should be evaluated on user-specific identity, near-neighbour negatives, open-set rejection and routing task loss rather than inheriting lenient CLIP coverage as confidence authority.

negative_results_and_rejects: Do not count the February Project-Frankenstein Adaptive Visual Pipeline as historical proof of online user-specific visual learning; it adapted route depth, not persistent class knowledge.
Do not count the later Drive Retina oracle-seeded dictionary as already satisfying GOLD/SILVER user-label admission, candidate-vs-current promotion, rollback or per-user scope.
Do not infer that FrankEye's frozen-head Retina-v8 inference weights imply an online update path; the code labels the CNN component inference-only.
Do not use the historical 'about 90% no VLM' code comment as a measured routing-savings fact without a corresponding benchmark receipt.
Do not equate lenient CLIP recognition/coverage with calibrated familiar identity or sensor truth.
